correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every rooted partial function obeying weak transitivity to one of five successor types: terminal, monochromatic looping, terminal child, different-colour loop child, or alternating two-cycle. By bisimulation the monochromatic nontrivial loops collapse to a single type. With q=2^k colours the disjoint families total q+q+q²+2q(q−1)=3q². Explicit depth-two formulas characterize each label; their disjunctions exhaust all subsets, proving a 2^(3·4^k) free-algebra cardinality for every k≥0, finite and infinite frames. A canonical 3q²-state model realizes all labels. Two colour-a worlds, one looping and one terminal-edge, agree to depth one but differ at depth two, proving optimality; mutually exclusive characteristics show the universal model size is minimal. Independent direct finite checking enumerated all partial maps of sizes ≤6 and 5,596,204 rooted binary-colour cases and verified characteristic formulas on canonical models for q=1,2,3. Finite tests do not replace general argument.

The earlier wK4 canonical-formula result supplies axiomatizability, not the 3·4^k five-family enumeration. Semantic searches of published mathematical records and general literature found no stronger exact comparison. A 2026 published published-finding corpus result characterizes partial-function frames in an unrelated marked measurable quotient problem, but has no weak-transitivity hypothesis nor quantified formula classes. A prior scientific statement classifies finite total-function frame-validity invariants, but no matching free-algebra statement. This supports originality within inspected scientific literature; older uninspected equivalent presentations remain a stated risk.

value.rationale: The all-rank free-algebra size is a natural exact invariant of an axiomatizable modal frame class at the intersection of two foundational properties, not a selected small census. The result supplies complete depth-two normal forms, optimal modal depth, and a smallest single semantic test model; this quantitatively strengthens qualitative local finiteness and provides exact syntactic expressivity bounds. Unlike total deterministic frames with arbitrary cycles/tails, the weak-transitivity hypothesis produces a sharp constant-depth collapse.
